subject: Private deployment: starter fee index, surge credits, and support windows
messages:
From: Kyle Harrison <kyle.harrison@mednex.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Amit Desai <amit.desai@mednex.com>

Subject: Private deployment: starter fee index, surge credits, and support windows

Hi David / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the tech looked solid. Our procurement and cloud teams asked for a few clarifications so we can finalize internal budget and timelines. Can you confirm the following from the commercial side?

1) Starter/platform fee amortization: your SOW currently shows the platform fee charged up-front. We prefer amortizing over a term. What options do you support (12 / 18 / 24 months)? Any impact to pricing if amortized?

2) Indexing approach: does the platform fee escalate? The legal team prefers an external index (CPI or similar) with an annual cap. What does Redwood propose?

3) Surge credits & burst capacity: our workloads have heavy month-to-month variance. Are there built-in burst credits or a surge pool? How do overage rates apply during peak months?

4) Support windows for private deployments: the SOW lists "Enterprise SRE" as an add-on. Can you outline standard on-call windows (regional business hours vs 24/7) and whether migration months carry different coverage?

I'm attaching the draft SOW with our marks (mednex_SOW_draft_v3.pdf) and an ops spreadsheet showing our anticipated month-by-month uplift (ops_window_matrix.xlsx).

If you can send a short commercial position on the four items above, that will help us move to procurement sign-off.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a short call if easier.

Thanks,
Kyle
Kyle Harrison
Head of Cloud Platforms | Mednex Health

On Thu, Dec 10, 2026 at 9:12 AM Kyle Harrison <kyle.harrison@mednex.com> wrote:
> Hi David / Marissa,
> 
> Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the tech looked solid. Our procurement and cloud teams asked for a few clarifications so we can finalize internal budget and timelines. Can you confirm the following from the commercial side?
> 
> 1) Starter/platform fee amortization...

Kyle — thanks for the clear notes and the attachments. Below is our commercial position for each ask; happy to adjust once we see your expected uplift numbers from the ops spreadsheet.

1) Starter/platform fee amortization:
- We can amortize the platform (starter) fee across 12, 18, or 24 months. Base price is unchanged; amortization only changes billing cadence.
- For 12-month amortization we typically require a 10% premium if there is no upfront commit (to cover short-term cash). For 18 months we can offer amortization at list with standard payment terms, and for 24 months we can offer a 3% price uplift discount since it smooths cash flow predictability.

2) Indexing approach:
- Our standard is annual adjustment tied to US CPI (Jan–Dec) with a configurable cap. Typical commercial practice we propose: CPI with a 6% cap and 0% floor (i.e., no negative adjustments).
- We can be flexible: for large enterprise deals we will accept a 3% floor and 6% cap (protects both sides). If you prefer a different external index we can consider, but CPI is simplest for both parties.

3) Surge credits & burst capacity:
- We provide a monthly burst credit pool tied to the commitment tier. Out of the box: 3 burst credits/month for Starter, 10 credits/month for Standard, and a flexible burst pool for Dedicated customers. Credits allow short-lived capacity increases up to X tokens/minute for brief peaks.
- Overage billing: 1) If monthly usage exceeds credits, overage billed at the agreed overage rate (typically 1.5x per-token list for bursts). 2) We offer a negotiated reduced overage rate if you purchase a burst buffer (pre-paid).
- If you anticipate sustained peaks in certain months, a hybrid (pre-paid burst buffer + dynamic routing to a lower-capacity model variant) tends to be the most cost-effective path.

4) Support windows for private deployments:
- Default: Business-hours regional support (Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 local) with 8-hour response for Sev2 and 24-hour for Sev3.
- Enterprise SRE add-on: 24/7 on-call (SRE) with 1-hour Sev1 response and on-call paging.
- Migration months (first 60–90 days) — we can include a temporary uplift of SRE coverage (covering the migration phase) as a committed item in the SOW (typically 4 weeks full-time equivalent, then tapered).

Next steps: If you can provide (a) the preferred amortization term (12/18/24), (b) a target overage budget or peak multiplier (e.g., +200% for three months), and (c) desired support during migration, we will produce a marked-up SOW and an alternate pricing schedule showing amortized billing and the burst buffer options.

I'll loop in Marissa and Olga for commercial sign-off on any concessions.

Best,
David Kim
Director, Commercials | Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Private deployment: starter fee index, surge credits, and support windows

Thanks David — that helps a lot. A few quick follow-ups and a counter proposal from our side:

- Amortization: we prefer 18-month amortization, aligned to our internal CAPEX schedule. We would ask that amortization be offered at list price (no premium).
- Indexing: we can accept CPI but would like a 3% floor and 8% cap (we're sensitive to inflation upside).
- Surge/overage: we see month-to-month spikes of ~2.5x baseline for two months during launches. Would you consider a lower overage multiplier (1.25x) if we commit to a 12-month minimum burst buffer (pre-paid)?
- Support: for the migration months we require 24/7 on-call for the first 90 days; after that we can step down to regional business hours.
- Pilot discount: procurement is asking for a limited pilot discount — 20% off platform fee for first six months to validate performance and TCO.

I've attached an annotated SOW with our redlines. Can your side run these items by finance/legal and come back with a concrete redline?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Kyle
[Attachment: mednex_SOW_draft_v3.pdf (annotated)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kyle Harrison <kyle.harrison@mednex.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment: starter fee index, surge credits, and support windows

Kyle — thanks for the clear counter. We've discussed internally with Finance and Legal; high level position below so we can keep momentum.

1) Amortization: 18-month amortization is acceptable to Redwood on this deal, provided the total committed ARR meets the MNX threshold in the term sheet. We will not apply an amortization premium for 18 months. We will include standard payment securities (net-30 payments + early-termination clawback schedule in the SOW).

2) Indexing: we can accept CPI with a 3% floor and a 6% cap. We cannot stretch to an 8% cap without pricing protection elsewhere (e.g., higher minimum commit or shorter amortization). If your finance team needs 8%, we would ask for a 12-month amortization and a 1% uplift to list to offset inflation exposure.

3) Surge & overage: we will offer the following middle ground:
- Pre-paid burst buffer for 12 months at a negotiated rate, with a reduced overage multiplier of 1.35x (instead of standard 1.5x) if you pre-pay the buffer.
- For the first 3 launch months we will temporarily increase the monthly burst credits by 2x (applied automatically) to cover expected spikes.

4) Support during migration: we will include 24/7 SRE coverage for the first 90 days at no additional charge as part of the onboarding package. After 90 days coverage steps down to regional business-hours unless you subscribe to the Enterprise SRE add-on.

5) Pilot discount: we can offer a pilot concession of 15% off the platform fee for the first four months (not six), conditional on a signed SOW and a minimum 12-month committed contract thereafter.

Next steps:
- We will prepare a redlined SOW reflecting the above (changes to amortization, indexing caps/floor, pre-paid burst buffer pricing, and the 90-day migration SRE clause).
- Proposed meeting: Legal + Procurement call on Monday 14 Dec at 10:00 PT to walk the SOW changes and agree final redlines. Please confirm attendees and I will send calendar invite.

If that sounds reasonable, David and I will produce the redline and loop in Legal.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Commercials | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
